subject: fix(web): give the member chip its own class
instruction:
fix(web): give the member chip its own class

`.ouro-chip` was the composer's "3 queued" count (W4) *and* the machines member
presence chip (W7). Because the machines block sits later in the file, the moment
that section became reachable its small-caps, its larger face and its grid
placement all landed on the queue count too.

Nobody had ever seen it, because the section had never been reachable: the
unterminated rule fixed two commits ago swallowed everything from the new-session
refusal to the end of the file. Repairing the stylesheet is what made this live —
so the repair introduced a visible regression in the composer, and this is it
being paid for rather than shipped.

Two components sharing one class name is the actual defect. They are not one
thing: a queue count is a fact about pacing in tertiary at 0.72rem, and a presence
chip is a semantic tone in small-caps that has to sit in a grid cell. The machines
family becomes `.ouro-member-chip{,-connected,-offline,-unknown}` and the composer
keeps the generic name it had first.

`StylesheetTest` grows the guard: a class claimed by more than one `/* ==== */`
section of the file fails, because that is two authors who did not know about each
other. Within one section it says nothing — `.ouro-composer-input` gets its box in
the focused-pane block and its behaviour in the composer block, and the deck's
media query restates three layout classes on purpose; that is one author working
on one thing.

The guard was checked against the bug rather than assumed to work: with
`.ouro-member-chip` renamed back to `.ouro-chip` it fails naming the class. The
first draft did not — it stripped comments before splitting on the section
banners, which are comments, leaving one undifferentiated section in which nothing
can collide.

Acceptance. These tests are restored into the worktree after the session ends and must pass:
  - the header uses it when the runtime gives one
  - and says nothing rather than inventing one when it does not
  - a blank or missing name reads as unnamed
  - a runtime with no fleet at all has no name to show
  - the page draws the name it was given, and the word Machines when it has none
  - this machine is connected even though the runtime never lists itself
  - this machine is connected before any status has arrived
  - a peer the status names is connected
  - a peer the status does not name is offline, once a status has arrived
  - a status that arrived naming nobody makes every peer offline, not unknown
  - before any status every peer is unknown rather than assumed offline
  - the counts are the presence rule's, not fleet.status's own summary

Rules. Files that already exist under `test/` must not be modified or deleted — the change is graded against tests restored from the history after the session ends. New test files of your own are allowed and are left in place. Work only inside this worktree.
